item.title: Suspect in deadly Lafayette stabbing apparently targeted victim
item.description: A troubling Facebook post has emerged suggesting the suspect in a deadly weekend stabbing in Lafayette may have targeted the victim.

item.title: San Jose braces for March Madness surge as Sweet 16, Elite Eight hit SAP Center
item.description: San Jose is preparing to host March Madness as the SAP Center welcomes the Sweet 16 on Thursday and the Elite Eight days later.

item.title: Oakland apartment fire that displaced 200 residents still unresolved
item.description: Tenants at at an Oakland apartment complex that burned in January are asking for relocation payments from their landlord. They say they are owed the money because there were code violations. The landlord says otherwise.

item.title: The Spear in San Francisco will be country's 1st 'office resort'
item.description: Presidio Bay Ventures is transforming 88 Spear into a first-of-its-kind office resort, featuring high-end amenities, a rooftop restaurant, and event space to attract workers and visitors downtown.

item.title: Catastrophic flooding in Hawaii sparks grassroots relief
item.description: Hawaii is experiencing some of its worst flooding in more than 20 years, leaving thousands without power and sweeping several homes off their foundations, authorities said.

item.title: Tractor trailer crashes, overturns on I-580 in Dublin, lanes blocked
item.description: The California Highway Patrol has issued a severe traffic alert on westbound Interstate 580 in Dublin Tuesday night. CHP says a jack-knifed tractor trailer overturned following a collision and is blocking three lanes of traffic.

item.title: Judge fines San Francisco public defender after finding him in contempt for refusing new cases
item.description: A judge has fined San Francisco's public defender $26,000 for ignoring a January order to stop rejecting cases — a pattern that critics say is straining the city's justice system.

item.title: Meta loses $375 million lawsuit to New Mexico AG
item.description: The New Mexico Attorney General's Office proved its case to a civil jury that awarded $375 million in damages. Meta's response though a spokesperson: “We respectfully disagree with the verdict and will appeal."

item.title: San Bruno police raise public safety concerns as contract talks stall
item.description: Officers say ongoing negotiations and lower pay could lead to departures and cuts to public safety services.

item.title: Last officer in Antioch, Pittsburg police corruption case sentenced
item.description: The last of 10 former Antioch and Pittsburg police officers charged in a wide-ranging corruption case was sentenced Tuesday to more than four years in federal prison.

item.title: Oakland high schooler wins cash for attendance
item.description: An Oakland high school freshman is being recognized — and rewarded — for showing up.

item.title: 2nd co-owner of San Jose daycare convicted in drowning deaths of toddlers
item.description: A former San Jose daycare co-owner whose negligence led to the deaths of two toddlers was convicted Tuesday of felony child endangerment, the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office said.

item.title: San Francisco trustees extend school year after teacher strike
item.description: The San Francisco Unified School District will extend its school year by one week this June to make up for instructional days lost during a teacher strike earlier this year.

item.title: Berkeley delays vote on $2M Flock surveillance expansion
item.description: Berkeley is postponing a decision on whether to expand and renew its contract with the Flock surveillance system after a marathon city council meeting.

item.title: TSA officials tip off ICE before arrest of Guatemalan mother at SFO: NYT
